=== V3 Orchestration-Free Roadmap ===
# Second Brain v3 — Orchestration-Free Roadmap

**Date:** 2026-09-23  
**Product boundary:** Harness-independent memory, context, knowledge, skills, and safe reuse. No Brain agent orchestrator.  
**Status:** Active candidate roadmap under the September 23 removal mandate; implementation and qualification are tracked separately in `M00-CAMPAIGN-REGISTER.md`. No production authorization.

## 1. Product goal

Make Second Brain inexpensive when it cannot help, and demonstrably useful when memory, knowledge, context, or procedural reuse can reduce repeated work.

The native harness decides who does work, which model is used, which tools may run, and when execution starts, stops, retries, or completes. Brain supplies the right permitted knowledge and preserves trustworthy memory. It does not own the task lifecycle.

Automatic context injection remains. Multiple agents can use one authorized knowledge base. Skills can become more discoverable, precise, reusable, and verifiable. None of those capabilities requires Brain to create agents, appoint a coordinator, or control their tools.

## 2. Architectural ownership

| Responsibility | Owner after removal |
|---|---|
| Agent creation, delegation, queues, retries, cancellation, completion | Native harness |
| Model/provider choice and agent-role configuration | User/native harness |
| Native tool permissions and execution isolation | Native harness and its supported security boundary |
| Canonical memory, retrieval, source knowledge, provenance | Brain |
| Context construction, injection, compaction continuity | Brain through a narrow host adapter |
| Skill discovery, approved content, recipes, provenance | Brain; execution remains with the host |
| Authorization for retained Brain data and privileged operations | Brain's retained permission/approval boundary |
| Usage/cost records | Brain may observe and aggregate supported evidence; it does not admit tasks |
| Index/cache/context/storage/local-compute limits | Brain for its own operations only |
| Host API differences | Thin compatibility adapters, not version-specific core behavior |

Correlation identifiers do not become privileged authority merely because they appear in a native event. Unknown usage and unknown provenance remain unknown. Core data integrity and approved-byte consumption are not removed with worker governance.

## 3. Explicit exclusions from all v3 plans

Remove coordinator recognition and custody improvements; protected worker issuance; driver/worker planes; agent or model routing; task admission; worker budget reservations; execution leases; completion/settlement/replay authority; native lifecycle supervision; agent scheduling/prefetch; worker recovery/resurrection; delegated coordinator hierarchies; and a multi-agent runtime.

Remove improvements to an orchestration handoff layer whose sole purpose is retaining those guarantees. Do not recreate them as a Brainstem executive, workflow engine, autonomous supervisor, resource governor, or cognitive operating system. Names do not change scope.

Preserve source/data lineage, memory authorization, and concurrent memory access even where their implementation previously shared files with orchestration. Retire the old feature, not unrelated data protections.

## 4. Development stages

The M00–M13 labels below map to the retrieved September 9 master roadmap. Later local plans may have reassigned responsibilities, especially M11/M12. Reconcile by capability against the actual active roadmap; preserve a documented mapping instead of silently renumbering history. These are modular increments, not a demand to create a tag for every stage.

### Stage 0 — Remove the redundant controller (M00 scope replacement)

Execute the accompanying removal mandate. Fix test-home isolation first. Remove both runtime and test-only governed behavior, retire obsolete tests and requirements, preserve applicable core protections, and independently review one frozen candidate.

**Finish:** One finite removal gate. No pending orchestration support commitment. No live activation implied.

### Stage 1 — Measurement and genuinely cheap runtime (M01, M02)

Capture native and Brain-enabled model-facing requests, full-turn timing, imports/startup, retrieval, injection, finalization, and resource usage. Keep native model and task settings matched so a model change cannot masquerade as a Brain improvement.

Implement the earliest useful local no-op decision, lazy initialization, bounded configuration reuse, and elimination of avoidable bridge/process work. A lifecycle component may manage Brain's own request processing or local resources; it may not become a native task/agent supervisor.

**Finish:** Controlled no-benefit requests add no Brain model-visible content or management calls and meet accepted local overhead budgets. Useful-memory negative controls establish that fast abstention did not simply stop recalling required knowledge.

### Stage 2 — Evidence-aware memory and safe reuse (M03, M04)

Represent source identity, revision, project scope, provenance, permissions, and freshness explicitly. Maintain one canonical memory authority with rebuildable views. Track dependencies so changed inputs invalidate affected derived knowledge and cached results without rebuilding everything.

A memory dependency graph describes evidence and derived data, not a distributed agent execution plan. Cache validation must cost less than the repeated work it avoids on the target workload.

**Finish:** Source, permission, corpus-membership, and relevant environment changes invalidate correctly; unchanged useful work is reused; acknowledged history survives interruption and upgrade.

### Stage 3 — Source discovery and precise retrieval (M05, M06)

Catalogue approved repositories, documents, mappings, assets, dumps, and existing project knowledge. Make their locations and useful access methods discoverable through natural requests. Compare suitable lexical, structural, and semantic retrieval operators using held-out project queries.

Discovery runs through permitted local indexing, ordinary host hooks, or explicitly invoked maintenance. Do not spawn Brain scout agents or add a discovery orchestrator.

**Finish:** Real domain tasks find and inspect the right permitted source; missing/stale/uncertain sources are reported honestly; wrong-project material is excluded; retrieval cost is measured.

### Stage 4 — Better context and durable continuity (M07)

Choose task-relevant exact, structured, extracted, or summarized views. Deduplicate within the actual recipient context without assuming that one agent's delivery reached every agent. Preserve required facts, constraints, and provenance through compaction and restart.

Retain context epochs and session/project correlation where needed. Those records describe memory delivery and recovery; they do not authorize dispatch or certify worker completion. Checkpoint acknowledged memory before reclaiming required context.

**Finish:** Less redundant context with no accepted loss of required information, no cross-project leakage, and correct recovery under native compaction/restart in the qualified host scope.

=== Orchestrator Removal Mandate ===
# Second Brain — Orchestrator Removal Mandate

**Date:** 2026-09-23  
**Direction:** Remove Second Brain's orchestration product surface; do not maintain a disabled implementation.  
**Execution boundary:** Candidate-only changes, tests, local commits, and independent review. No production activation, canonical-state migration, push, tag, global OS change, or installed-host patch.  
**Status:** Execution instruction derived from the user's direction, not an implementation or qualification result.

## 1. Product decision

Second Brain is a harness-independent memory, context, knowledge, skills, and reuse system. The native harness owns agent creation, model selection, delegation, tools, execution permissions, scheduling, cancellation, retries, and task lifecycle.

Remove Brain's orchestrator rather than improving its handoff, maintaining native/governed dual modes, or preserving a test-only governed runtime. This instruction supersedes the previous choice to keep governed orchestration runnable through test switches. Orchestration improvements are out of the v3 product scope, not postponed prerequisites.

Agents may still use shared Brain knowledge, receive automatic context, retrieve approved skills, and write memory through authorized interfaces. Multiple native agents using Brain is supported consumption of a shared service, not permission to rebuild an agent controller.

Keep core behavior version-independent. Normalize host-specific inputs behind adapters. Do not bind core semantics to OMP/OpenCode/Hermes versions, internal classes, event names, role labels, or model/provider identities. Exact artifact identities still matter for testing; version independence is not an exemption from qualification.

## 2. Authority and source precedence

The user's September 23 report describes the latest candidate: extension 786 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed; Python 2,373 passed / 7 skipped / 8 failed. The report attributes eight failures to earlier work, with four explicitly rerun against committed HEAD. These are reported results, not independently reproduced results in this document. The Python suite is not green.

The current local worktree is the implementation source of truth. The report identifies `.worktrees/m00.3-producer-guard`; verify the repository, branch, interpreter, and actual files before editing. Do not mistake the parent checkout's prompt for the candidate identity.

Archived roadmap/register copies are historical planning evidence. Where they demand orchestration repair, this product decision supersedes that demand. Preserve their historical verdicts and failed evidence rather than rewriting history as successful qualification.

Proceed with the candidate-local removal and the bounded work below without requesting another authorization merely to remove the retired feature. Existing restrictions on production, protected state, paid work, and privileged execution remain in force.

## 3. Immediate containment and preservation

Before another suite runs, fix `worker-context.test.ts` and audit the relevant test setup and child-process launches for real-home fallback. Every test that can load Brain must use an explicit disposable home, candidate source/interpreter, isolated working files, and isolated configuration. Clear inherited `PYTHONPATH` and `PYTHONHOME` before deliberately supplying any candidate-local import path. Apply the isolation to subprocesses, not just the parent runner. Assert the resolved import origin and data-home path.

Check the possible earlier real-home contact using read-only, consistent evidence. Do not restore an old backup over legitimate newer state. Distinguish no intentional activation from proof of no data writes. If no suitable before-state exists, report that retrospective preservation is not proven. This investigation must not become a new orchestration project.

Inventory tracked and untracked candidate changes, including pre-existing lineage and skill-approval work. Preserve other authors' changes and identify dependencies. Do not use blanket staging, destructive resets, or cleanup of unknown files. Record a compact patch/hash manifest; do not create redundant repository, database, or worktree copies merely for documentation.

## 4. Remove the execution-control surface

Remove executable implementations, imports, registrations, prompts, hooks, command wiring, packaging, and active tests whose sole purpose is:

- Brain driver/orchestrator/coordinator role creation, model allowlists, or privileged coordinator admission.
- Agent/worker dispatch, task scheduling, lifecycle mirroring, completion authority, replay authority, execution leases, reservation/settlement, cleanup barriers, or worker resurrection.
- Brain enforcement of native tool access, model/role assignment, worker budgets, or host task STOP/cancellation policy.
- Protected coordinator issuer/bootstrap/custody work that exists exclusively to support these removed operations.
- Native/governed mode selection, `governedOrchestrationForTests`, `worker_protocol._GOVERNED_FOR_TESTS`, and equivalent alternate activation paths.

Use dependency analysis, not filename deletion. A module named `governor`, `worker_context`, `contracts`, or `lineage` may also contain retained functionality. Extract or preserve that functionality, then remove the retired branches. Do not preserve a working retired engine because a shared helper is useful.

Do not replace the engine with a wrapper scheduler, second supervisor, native-handoff controller, or a renamed cognitive executive. Do not patch native harnesses to replace guarantees that Brain no longer offers.

### Retain only minimal compatibility where necessary

Unregister retired APIs wherever possible. A still-reachable legacy command may be a small inert refusal returning an explicit removed/unsupported result, with no dispatch, privilege grant, fabricated completion, reservation, or data mutation. It must not import or initialize the retired engine. No environment variable, config option, CLI argument, or test flag may reactivate it.

Ordinary memory/context loading must not require orchestration configuration. A missing legacy `mode` must not break loading. Old orchestration-only configuration may produce a bounded deprecation diagnostic but cannot activate execution governance. Preserve validation of unrelated retained settings. Specify the compatibility behavior and test it once; do not retain two runtime profiles.

Do not drop historical orchestration tables, receipts, artifacts, or migrations simply to remove runtime code. Retain them as historical data where needed, without active enforcement. Do not fabricate completion, settlement, release, or refunded capacity for old rows. Any future production cutover must account for live work and current data without destructive downgrade; that does not authorize rebuilding a census or custody subsystem in this campaign.

## 5. Preserve the useful Brain

Preserve automatic context injection, retrieval, canonical memory, provenance, knowledge/source discovery, project/session isolation, approved skill consumption, safe reuse, compaction checkpoints, and recovery of memory/context.

=== V3 Orchestration-Free Roadmap ===
# Second Brain v3 — Orchestration-Free Roadmap

**Date:** 2026-09-23  
**Product boundary:** Harness-independent memory, context, knowledge, skills, and safe reuse. No Brain agent orchestrator.  
**Status:** Active candidate roadmap under the September 23 removal mandate; implementation and qualification are tracked separately in `M00-CAMPAIGN-REGISTER.md`. No production authorization.

## 1. Product goal

Make Second Brain inexpensive when it cannot help, and demonstrably useful when memory, knowledge, context, or procedural reuse can reduce repeated work.

The native harness decides who does work, which model is used, which tools may run, and when execution starts, stops, retries, or completes. Brain supplies the right permitted knowledge and preserves trustworthy memory. It does not own the task lifecycle.

Automatic context injection remains. Multiple agents can use one authorized knowledge base. Skills can become more discoverable, precise, reusable, and verifiable. None of those capabilities requires Brain to create agents, appoint a coordinator, or control their tools.

## 2. Architectural ownership

| Responsibility | Owner after removal |
|---|---|
| Agent creation, delegation, queues, retries, cancellation, completion | Native harness |
| Model/provider choice and agent-role configuration | User/native harness |
| Native tool permissions and execution isolation | Native harness and its supported security boundary |
| Canonical memory, retrieval, source knowledge, provenance | Brain |
| Context construction, injection, compaction continuity | Brain through a narrow host adapter |
| Skill discovery, approved content, recipes, provenance | Brain; execution remains with the host |
| Authorization for retained Brain data and privileged operations | Brain's retained permission/approval boundary |
| Usage/cost records | Brain may observe and aggregate supported evidence; it does not admit tasks |
| Index/cache/context/storage/local-compute limits | Brain for its own operations only |
| Host API differences | Thin compatibility adapters, not version-specific core behavior |

Correlation identifiers do not become privileged authority merely because they appear in a native event. Unknown usage and unknown provenance remain unknown. Core data integrity and approved-byte consumption are not removed with worker governance.

## 3. Explicit exclusions from all v3 plans

Remove coordinator recognition and custody improvements; protected worker issuance; driver/worker planes; agent or model routing; task admission; worker budget reservations; execution leases; completion/settlement/replay authority; native lifecycle supervision; agent scheduling/prefetch; worker recovery/resurrection; delegated coordinator hierarchies; and a multi-agent runtime.

Remove improvements to an orchestration handoff layer whose sole purpose is retaining those guarantees. Do not recreate them as a Brainstem executive, workflow engine, autonomous supervisor, resource governor, or cognitive operating system. Names do not change scope.

Preserve source/data lineage, memory authorization, and concurrent memory access even where their implementation previously shared files with orchestration. Retire the old feature, not unrelated data protections.

## 4. Development stages

The M00–M13 labels below map to the retrieved September 9 master roadmap. Later local plans may have reassigned responsibilities, especially M11/M12. Reconcile by capability against the actual active roadmap; preserve a documented mapping instead of silently renumbering history. These are modular increments, not a demand to create a tag for every stage.

### Stage 0 — Remove the redundant controller (M00 scope replacement)

Execute the accompanying removal mandate. Fix test-home isolation first. Remove both runtime and test-only governed behavior, retire obsolete tests and requirements, preserve applicable core protections, and independently review one frozen candidate.

**Finish:** One finite removal gate. No pending orchestration support commitment. No live activation implied.

### Stage 1 — Measurement and genuinely cheap runtime (M01, M02)

Capture native and Brain-enabled model-facing requests, full-turn timing, imports/startup, retrieval, injection, finalization, and resource usage. Keep native model and task settings matched so a model change cannot masquerade as a Brain improvement.

Implement the earliest useful local no-op decision, lazy initialization, bounded configuration reuse, and elimination of avoidable bridge/process work. A lifecycle component may manage Brain's own request processing or local resources; it may not become a native task/agent supervisor.

**Finish:** Controlled no-benefit requests add no Brain model-visible content or management calls and meet accepted local overhead budgets. Useful-memory negative controls establish that fast abstention did not simply stop recalling required knowledge.

### Stage 2 — Evidence-aware memory and safe reuse (M03, M04)

Represent source identity, revision, project scope, provenance, permissions, and freshness explicitly. Maintain one canonical memory authority with rebuildable views. Track dependencies so changed inputs invalidate affected derived knowledge and cached results without rebuilding everything.

A memory dependency graph describes evidence and derived data, not a distributed agent execution plan. Cache validation must cost less than the repeated work it avoids on the target workload.

**Finish:** Source, permission, corpus-membership, and relevant environment changes invalidate correctly; unchanged useful work is reused; acknowledged history survives interruption and upgrade.

### Stage 3 — Source discovery and precise retrieval (M05, M06)

Catalogue approved repositories, documents, mappings, assets, dumps, and existing project knowledge. Make their locations and useful access methods discoverable through natural requests. Compare suitable lexical, structural, and semantic retrieval operators using held-out project queries.

Discovery runs through permitted local indexing, ordinary host hooks, or explicitly invoked maintenance. Do not spawn Brain scout agents or add a discovery orchestrator.

**Finish:** Real domain tasks find and inspect the right permitted source; missing/stale/uncertain sources are reported honestly; wrong-project material is excluded; retrieval cost is measured.

### Stage 4 — Better context and durable continuity (M07)

Choose task-relevant exact, structured, extracted, or summarized views. Deduplicate within the actual recipient context without assuming that one agent's delivery reached every agent. Preserve required facts, constraints, and provenance through compaction and restart.

Retain context epochs and session/project correlation where needed. Those records describe memory delivery and recovery; they do not authorize dispatch or certify worker completion. Checkpoint acknowledged memory before reclaiming required context.

**Finish:** Less redundant context with no accepted loss of required information, no cross-project leakage, and correct recovery under native compaction/restart in the qualified host scope.

=== Orchestrator Removal Mandate ===
# Second Brain — Orchestrator Removal Mandate

**Date:** 2026-09-23  
**Direction:** Remove Second Brain's orchestration product surface; do not maintain a disabled implementation.  
**Execution boundary:** Candidate-only changes, tests, local commits, and independent review. No production activation, canonical-state migration, push, tag, global OS change, or installed-host patch.  
**Status:** Execution instruction derived from the user's direction, not an implementation or qualification result.

## 1. Product decision

Second Brain is a harness-independent memory, context, knowledge, skills, and reuse system. The native harness owns agent creation, model selection, delegation, tools, execution permissions, scheduling, cancellation, retries, and task lifecycle.

Remove Brain's orchestrator rather than improving its handoff, maintaining native/governed dual modes, or preserving a test-only governed runtime. This instruction supersedes the previous choice to keep governed orchestration runnable through test switches. Orchestration improvements are out of the v3 product scope, not postponed prerequisites.

Agents may still use shared Brain knowledge, receive automatic context, retrieve approved skills, and write memory through authorized interfaces. Multiple native agents using Brain is supported consumption of a shared service, not permission to rebuild an agent controller.

Keep core behavior version-independent. Normalize host-specific inputs behind adapters. Do not bind core semantics to OMP/OpenCode/Hermes versions, internal classes, event names, role labels, or model/provider identities. Exact artifact identities still matter for testing; version independence is not an exemption from qualification.

## 2. Authority and source precedence

The user's September 23 report describes the latest candidate: extension 786 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed; Python 2,373 passed / 7 skipped / 8 failed. The report attributes eight failures to earlier work, with four explicitly rerun against committed HEAD. These are reported results, not independently reproduced results in this document. The Python suite is not green.

The current local worktree is the implementation source of truth. The report identifies `.worktrees/m00.3-producer-guard`; verify the repository, branch, interpreter, and actual files before editing. Do not mistake the parent checkout's prompt for the candidate identity.

Archived roadmap/register copies are historical planning evidence. Where they demand orchestration repair, this product decision supersedes that demand. Preserve their historical verdicts and failed evidence rather than rewriting history as successful qualification.

Proceed with the candidate-local removal and the bounded work below without requesting another authorization merely to remove the retired feature. Existing restrictions on production, protected state, paid work, and privileged execution remain in force.

## 3. Immediate containment and preservation

Before another suite runs, fix `worker-context.test.ts` and audit the relevant test setup and child-process launches for real-home fallback. Every test that can load Brain must use an explicit disposable home, candidate source/interpreter, isolated working files, and isolated configuration. Clear inherited `PYTHONPATH` and `PYTHONHOME` before deliberately supplying any candidate-local import path. Apply the isolation to subprocesses, not just the parent runner. Assert the resolved import origin and data-home path.

Check the possible earlier real-home contact using read-only, consistent evidence. Do not restore an old backup over legitimate newer state. Distinguish no intentional activation from proof of no data writes. If no suitable before-state exists, report that retrospective preservation is not proven. This investigation must not become a new orchestration project.

Inventory tracked and untracked candidate changes, including pre-existing lineage and skill-approval work. Preserve other authors' changes and identify dependencies. Do not use blanket staging, destructive resets, or cleanup of unknown files. Record a compact patch/hash manifest; do not create redundant repository, database, or worktree copies merely for documentation.

## 4. Remove the execution-control surface

Remove executable implementations, imports, registrations, prompts, hooks, command wiring, packaging, and active tests whose sole purpose is:

- Brain driver/orchestrator/coordinator role creation, model allowlists, or privileged coordinator admission.
- Agent/worker dispatch, task scheduling, lifecycle mirroring, completion authority, replay authority, execution leases, reservation/settlement, cleanup barriers, or worker resurrection.
- Brain enforcement of native tool access, model/role assignment, worker budgets, or host task STOP/cancellation policy.
- Protected coordinator issuer/bootstrap/custody work that exists exclusively to support these removed operations.
- Native/governed mode selection, `governedOrchestrationForTests`, `worker_protocol._GOVERNED_FOR_TESTS`, and equivalent alternate activation paths.

Use dependency analysis, not filename deletion. A module named `governor`, `worker_context`, `contracts`, or `lineage` may also contain retained functionality. Extract or preserve that functionality, then remove the retired branches. Do not preserve a working retired engine because a shared helper is useful.

Do not replace the engine with a wrapper scheduler, second supervisor, native-handoff controller, or a renamed cognitive executive. Do not patch native harnesses to replace guarantees that Brain no longer offers.

### Retain only minimal compatibility where necessary

Unregister retired APIs wherever possible. A still-reachable legacy command may be a small inert refusal returning an explicit removed/unsupported result, with no dispatch, privilege grant, fabricated completion, reservation, or data mutation. It must not import or initialize the retired engine. No environment variable, config option, CLI argument, or test flag may reactivate it.

Ordinary memory/context loading must not require orchestration configuration. A missing legacy `mode` must not break loading. Old orchestration-only configuration may produce a bounded deprecation diagnostic but cannot activate execution governance. Preserve validation of unrelated retained settings. Specify the compatibility behavior and test it once; do not retain two runtime profiles.

Do not drop historical orchestration tables, receipts, artifacts, or migrations simply to remove runtime code. Retain them as historical data where needed, without active enforcement. Do not fabricate completion, settlement, release, or refunded capacity for old rows. Any future production cutover must account for live work and current data without destructive downgrade; that does not authorize rebuilding a census or custody subsystem in this campaign.

## 5. Preserve the useful Brain

Preserve automatic context injection, retrieval, canonical memory, provenance, knowledge/source discovery, project/session isolation, approved skill consumption, safe reuse, compaction checkpoints, and recovery of memory/context.

=== V3 Orchestration-Free Roadmap ===
# Second Brain v3 — Orchestration-Free Roadmap

**Date:** 2026-09-23  
**Product boundary:** Harness-independent memory, context, knowledge, skills, and safe reuse. No Brain agent orchestrator.  
**Status:** Active candidate roadmap under the September 23 removal mandate; implementation and qualification are tracked separately in `M00-CAMPAIGN-REGISTER.md`. No production authorization.

## 1. Product goal

Make Second Brain inexpensive when it cannot help, and demonstrably useful when memory, knowledge, context, or procedural reuse can reduce repeated work.

The native harness decides who does work, which model is used, which tools may run, and when execution starts, stops, retries, or completes. Brain supplies the right permitted knowledge and preserves trustworthy memory. It does not own the task lifecycle.

Automatic context injection remains. Multiple agents can use one authorized knowledge base. Skills can become more discoverable, precise, reusable, and verifiable. None of those capabilities requires Brain to create agents, appoint a coordinator, or control their tools.

## 2. Architectural ownership

| Responsibility | Owner after removal |
|---|---|
| Agent creation, delegation, queues, retries, cancellation, completion | Native harness |
| Model/provider choice and agent-role configuration | User/native harness |
| Native tool permissions and execution isolation | Native harness and its supported security boundary |
| Canonical memory, retrieval, source knowledge, provenance | Brain |
| Context construction, injection, compaction continuity | Brain through a narrow host adapter |
| Skill discovery, approved content, recipes, provenance | Brain; execution remains with the host |
| Authorization for retained Brain data and privileged operations | Brain's retained permission/approval boundary |
| Usage/cost records | Brain may observe and aggregate supported evidence; it does not admit tasks |
| Index/cache/context/storage/local-compute limits | Brain for its own operations only |
| Host API differences | Thin compatibility adapters, not version-specific core behavior |

Correlation identifiers do not become privileged authority merely because they appear in a native event. Unknown usage and unknown provenance remain unknown. Core data integrity and approved-byte consumption are not removed with worker governance.

## 3. Explicit exclusions from all v3 plans

Remove coordinator recognition and custody improvements; protected worker issuance; driver/worker planes; agent or model routing; task admission; worker budget reservations; execution leases; completion/settlement/replay authority; native lifecycle supervision; agent scheduling/prefetch; worker recovery/resurrection; delegated coordinator hierarchies; and a multi-agent runtime.

Remove improvements to an orchestration handoff layer whose sole purpose is retaining those guarantees. Do not recreate them as a Brainstem executive, workflow engine, autonomous supervisor, resource governor, or cognitive operating system. Names do not change scope.

Preserve source/data lineage, memory authorization, and concurrent memory access even where their implementation previously shared files with orchestration. Retire the old feature, not unrelated data protections.

## 4. Development stages

The M00–M13 labels below map to the retrieved September 9 master roadmap. Later local plans may have reassigned responsibilities, especially M11/M12. Reconcile by capability against the actual active roadmap; preserve a documented mapping instead of silently renumbering history. These are modular increments, not a demand to create a tag for every stage.

### Stage 0 — Remove the redundant controller (M00 scope replacement)

Execute the accompanying removal mandate. Fix test-home isolation first. Remove both runtime and test-only governed behavior, retire obsolete tests and requirements, preserve applicable core protections, and independently review one frozen candidate.

**Finish:** One finite removal gate. No pending orchestration support commitment. No live activation implied.

### Stage 1 — Measurement and genuinely cheap runtime (M01, M02)

Capture native and Brain-enabled model-facing requests, full-turn timing, imports/startup, retrieval, injection, finalization, and resource usage. Keep native model and task settings matched so a model change cannot masquerade as a Brain improvement.

Implement the earliest useful local no-op decision, lazy initialization, bounded configuration reuse, and elimination of avoidable bridge/process work. A lifecycle component may manage Brain's own request processing or local resources; it may not become a native task/agent supervisor.

**Finish:** Controlled no-benefit requests add no Brain model-visible content or management calls and meet accepted local overhead budgets. Useful-memory negative controls establish that fast abstention did not simply stop recalling required knowledge.

### Stage 2 — Evidence-aware memory and safe reuse (M03, M04)

Represent source identity, revision, project scope, provenance, permissions, and freshness explicitly. Maintain one canonical memory authority with rebuildable views. Track dependencies so changed inputs invalidate affected derived knowledge and cached results without rebuilding everything.

A memory dependency graph describes evidence and derived data, not a distributed agent execution plan. Cache validation must cost less than the repeated work it avoids on the target workload.

**Finish:** Source, permission, corpus-membership, and relevant environment changes invalidate correctly; unchanged useful work is reused; acknowledged history survives interruption and upgrade.

### Stage 3 — Source discovery and precise retrieval (M05, M06)

Catalogue approved repositories, documents, mappings, assets, dumps, and existing project knowledge. Make their locations and useful access methods discoverable through natural requests. Compare suitable lexical, structural, and semantic retrieval operators using held-out project queries.

Discovery runs through permitted local indexing, ordinary host hooks, or explicitly invoked maintenance. Do not spawn Brain scout agents or add a discovery orchestrator.

**Finish:** Real domain tasks find and inspect the right permitted source; missing/stale/uncertain sources are reported honestly; wrong-project material is excluded; retrieval cost is measured.

### Stage 4 — Better context and durable continuity (M07)

Choose task-relevant exact, structured, extracted, or summarized views. Deduplicate within the actual recipient context without assuming that one agent's delivery reached every agent. Preserve required facts, constraints, and provenance through compaction and restart.

Retain context epochs and session/project correlation where needed. Those records describe memory delivery and recovery; they do not authorize dispatch or certify worker completion. Checkpoint acknowledged memory before reclaiming required context.

**Finish:** Less redundant context with no accepted loss of required information, no cross-project leakage, and correct recovery under native compaction/restart in the qualified host scope.

=== Orchestrator Removal Mandate ===
# Second Brain — Orchestrator Removal Mandate

**Date:** 2026-09-23  
**Direction:** Remove Second Brain's orchestration product surface; do not maintain a disabled implementation.  
**Execution boundary:** Candidate-only changes, tests, local commits, and independent review. No production activation, canonical-state migration, push, tag, global OS change, or installed-host patch.  
**Status:** Execution instruction derived from the user's direction, not an implementation or qualification result.

## 1. Product decision

Second Brain is a harness-independent memory, context, knowledge, skills, and reuse system. The native harness owns agent creation, model selection, delegation, tools, execution permissions, scheduling, cancellation, retries, and task lifecycle.

Remove Brain's orchestrator rather than improving its handoff, maintaining native/governed dual modes, or preserving a test-only governed runtime. This instruction supersedes the previous choice to keep governed orchestration runnable through test switches. Orchestration improvements are out of the v3 product scope, not postponed prerequisites.

Agents may still use shared Brain knowledge, receive automatic context, retrieve approved skills, and write memory through authorized interfaces. Multiple native agents using Brain is supported consumption of a shared service, not permission to rebuild an agent controller.

Keep core behavior version-independent. Normalize host-specific inputs behind adapters. Do not bind core semantics to OMP/OpenCode/Hermes versions, internal classes, event names, role labels, or model/provider identities. Exact artifact identities still matter for testing; version independence is not an exemption from qualification.

## 2. Authority and source precedence

The user's September 23 report describes the latest candidate: extension 786 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed; Python 2,373 passed / 7 skipped / 8 failed. The report attributes eight failures to earlier work, with four explicitly rerun against committed HEAD. These are reported results, not independently reproduced results in this document. The Python suite is not green.

The current local worktree is the implementation source of truth. The report identifies `.worktrees/m00.3-producer-guard`; verify the repository, branch, interpreter, and actual files before editing. Do not mistake the parent checkout's prompt for the candidate identity.

Archived roadmap/register copies are historical planning evidence. Where they demand orchestration repair, this product decision supersedes that demand. Preserve their historical verdicts and failed evidence rather than rewriting history as successful qualification.

Proceed with the candidate-local removal and the bounded work below without requesting another authorization merely to remove the retired feature. Existing restrictions on production, protected state, paid work, and privileged execution remain in force.

## 3. Immediate containment and preservation

Before another suite runs, fix `worker-context.test.ts` and audit the relevant test setup and child-process launches for real-home fallback. Every test that can load Brain must use an explicit disposable home, candidate source/interpreter, isolated working files, and isolated configuration. Clear inherited `PYTHONPATH` and `PYTHONHOME` before deliberately supplying any candidate-local import path. Apply the isolation to subprocesses, not just the parent runner. Assert the resolved import origin and data-home path.

Check the possible earlier real-home contact using read-only, consistent evidence. Do not restore an old backup over legitimate newer state. Distinguish no intentional activation from proof of no data writes. If no suitable before-state exists, report that retrospective preservation is not proven. This investigation must not become a new orchestration project.

Inventory tracked and untracked candidate changes, including pre-existing lineage and skill-approval work. Preserve other authors' changes and identify dependencies. Do not use blanket staging, destructive resets, or cleanup of unknown files. Record a compact patch/hash manifest; do not create redundant repository, database, or worktree copies merely for documentation.

## 4. Remove the execution-control surface

Remove executable implementations, imports, registrations, prompts, hooks, command wiring, packaging, and active tests whose sole purpose is:

- Brain driver/orchestrator/coordinator role creation, model allowlists, or privileged coordinator admission.
- Agent/worker dispatch, task scheduling, lifecycle mirroring, completion authority, replay authority, execution leases, reservation/settlement, cleanup barriers, or worker resurrection.
- Brain enforcement of native tool access, model/role assignment, worker budgets, or host task STOP/cancellation policy.
- Protected coordinator issuer/bootstrap/custody work that exists exclusively to support these removed operations.
- Native/governed mode selection, `governedOrchestrationForTests`, `worker_protocol._GOVERNED_FOR_TESTS`, and equivalent alternate activation paths.

Use dependency analysis, not filename deletion. A module named `governor`, `worker_context`, `contracts`, or `lineage` may also contain retained functionality. Extract or preserve that functionality, then remove the retired branches. Do not preserve a working retired engine because a shared helper is useful.

Do not replace the engine with a wrapper scheduler, second supervisor, native-handoff controller, or a renamed cognitive executive. Do not patch native harnesses to replace guarantees that Brain no longer offers.

### Retain only minimal compatibility where necessary

Unregister retired APIs wherever possible. A still-reachable legacy command may be a small inert refusal returning an explicit removed/unsupported result, with no dispatch, privilege grant, fabricated completion, reservation, or data mutation. It must not import or initialize the retired engine. No environment variable, config option, CLI argument, or test flag may reactivate it.

Ordinary memory/context loading must not require orchestration configuration. A missing legacy `mode` must not break loading. Old orchestration-only configuration may produce a bounded deprecation diagnostic but cannot activate execution governance. Preserve validation of unrelated retained settings. Specify the compatibility behavior and test it once; do not retain two runtime profiles.

Do not drop historical orchestration tables, receipts, artifacts, or migrations simply to remove runtime code. Retain them as historical data where needed, without active enforcement. Do not fabricate completion, settlement, release, or refunded capacity for old rows. Any future production cutover must account for live work and current data without destructive downgrade; that does not authorize rebuilding a census or custody subsystem in this campaign.

## 5. Preserve the useful Brain

Preserve automatic context injection, retrieval, canonical memory, provenance, knowledge/source discovery, project/session isolation, approved skill consumption, safe reuse, compaction checkpoints, and recovery of memory/context.
